Ok, first off the cell phone mounts on the wall that you can use to record your climbs... GENIUS! Why more gyms don't do this I don't know but I love it.

The gym is small, but in that small space they pack in a good mix of climbing styles and routes. This is bouldering only, but you'll still get a decent workout here regardless.

Now for the not so hot points; it's a small gym and a lot of the current routes at the time of this review didn't feel like a challenge to me. I'm not an expert, but I am tall and I was able to literally reach for the last hold on most of the routes. Granted not a big issue, but the routes that were marked as hard certainly held up to that rating. At the end of the day I felt like it was a good workout, but was also left wanting more.

If you're a new climber or you're looking to get your fingers chalky check this gym out! That being said, if you're a seasoned gripper you may want to do a day pass here and possibly try another gym if you don't feel challenged.

I really hope Rock On sticks around, this city needs more gyms and there's certainty a lot of promise here. I'm Looking forward to coming back again.

Now, enter our group of 15 to 20 people, all looking for some good beer and a place to chat. We picked Henderson's because we were all fans of the beer... Sadly this is no longer the case for myself as the wait staff that evening was less than impressed with out Mac Donald's food orgy.

It also just so happened that day Henderson's was hosting a small vegan restaurant inside - so I guess this was just the wrong day to wheel in some 15 orders of artery clogging, mashed animal "meat". That being said, if you're going to have a house rule to allow outside food, you can't get picky about what outside food is brought in.

Anyway; I was sure to tip the waitress who looked the most angry with a tip that was basically three times what I ordered (a single beer). This hostel is great if you're traveling alone! Friendly staff and the place is kept clean and well organized. While I did feel that the hostel is smaller than what I saw in the photos... this is Japan, so don't expect a palace. The rooms are also kept nice and while I did get a good nights sleep each night there is a elementary school across the road that does these "morning exercises". If you have your window open and are a light sleeper, you will be woken up by this so bring headphones and or ear plugs as a precaution.

The location of the hostel is really great. You only need to walk about 15-20 minutes to get into the core of Osaka. I'd personally only use the public transit for day trips to a far area of the city and or on your arrival/exit date. If you have a JR pass you *can* walk to the hostel from the station, but it is a bit of a trek and the metro will only cost you about $1.50 to go one stop to where the hostel is.

If you're looking for a great local bar I strongly recommend "Bar Blackon バー ブラコン 黒紺" which is about a short walk away. The guy running that place doesn't speak much English, but he did give us a great time! Its only big enough for five people, so choose who you take with you.

Overall I had a great time at this hostel, with one slight issue... It is a bit hard to meet people without the "traditional" hostel happy hour. The hostel could benefit from having just a few social events such as simple walking tours around the area and or just a typical hangout kind of event for anyone who wants meet some folks and or is traveling alone. That being said, I know these things take extra effort on the hostels part so its not so much a failing as it is a thing of note.

properties.review_text_published:
This hostel is so nice they're just giving away beds on the daily!

I had booked a room days in advance, checked in, and dropped all my stuff in the room only to come back late at night and find another guy sleeping in my assigned bed. This fellow had appearently checked out the day before but for some reason had full access to the room and as a result my bed.

Both of us were not into spooning for the night and thankfully the hostel did find me a staff room to sleep in for the night. That being said, the whole experience just threw a wrench into what was otherwise a very pleasant vacation. I don't know who would be to blame in this case, but the hostel needs to do a better job controlling access to the rooms rather than just giving every guest the same pin code... Perhaps an actual key? 🤯

The only positive thing I can say was that the staff did sort out the situation pretty quickly and I got a full refund for my stay. I was also allowed to keep a bag there while I waited to check into the next place which was nice.

The other issue not related to bed sharing is the location, it's a bit weird to get to given construction works and that it's kind of out of the way. This is less of an issue for some and not really one for me either, but people should be aware of this when staying here.

While I didn't enjoy my stay, it seems others do and to the hostels credit it is a nice place... I wish I could have had the chance to try it out.

properties.review_text_published:
Long story short I was looking for a place that was low key and had some sort of spa. Do C had it. The sauna is 24 hours so you can drop by whenever you're able to. The added bonus is that this capsule hotel has well... Capsules!

I liked my stay here, but a few things could be improved. Chief of which are the capsules themselves. It looks like this used to be an old school capsule hotel and the pods are right out of the 1980's. That being said I did have a comfortable sleep and while I'm six foot five inches tall (196cm est.) I did fit inside. I you're also my height of recommend sleeping diagonally which works pretty good too. Speaking of sleep, bring your own ear plugs as you may hear your neighbor(s).

The sauna and the hotel itself has a unique look, all decked out in plywood and concrete. You really fell secluded when you stay here and it's nearly isolated completely from the outside world. The hotel is clean and the minimalist design really enhances that as well. The staff is friendly, but getting answers quickly online doesn't seem to be a thing. Not a big deal, but the website should have some of those basic questions so that one doesn't need to scan through reviews.

Overall it was exactly what I was looking for in my stay and I'm glad I picked Do C for my last night in Tokyo. After a long trip it was nice to fully unwind and relax.

Fantastic hostel! So not only was the price fair, but this hostel is pretty social most nights and should there not be anyone around the staff is very friendly too. There are some social events if sparking conversation isn't your thing, plus a happy hour if you need some liquid courage.

The hostel is located near two stations that easily take you anywhere in Vienna and despite this, the hostel is very quiet at night thanks to it being off on a side street AND the they close some areas at night so things don't get too rowdy.

properties.review_text_published:
Come one, come all to another cannabis shop on Queen Street. Unlike the the other one (located near University Ave.) Nova Cannabis never really has a line up! Shocking, I know! Just show your ID and walk inside.

What you'll find is all the strains categorized by type (sativa, indica, hybrid, etc.) along one wall and all your "tools" in glass cases at the back as well. It feels like an Apple store only, but unlike Macs and iPhones the products here won't require you to remortgage your home.

Prices are the same as you'd find online or at other stores because cheap weed is usually mixed with stuff you don't want in you. Personally I like the Campfire strain, but if you're new or unsure just ask one of the "budtenders" inside and they'll sort you out.

Overall I found the store nice and the staff were knowledgeable about the products for sale as well as what vaporizers are good for beginners or what the THC and CBD percentages mean. All in all it's a great store to visit if the line up outside the other one is too long.

PS: Legalization is a touchy issue, take every negative review with a grain of salt. Every legal store will sell more or less the same products at the same price. What matters is the knowledge the staff has and of course that the cannabis is safe for consumption (which any street dealer can never verify).

properties.review_text_published:
Rarely do I go back to re-review a place when I have a bad experience, but congratulations Tango Palace, you've made the list!

To be honest I don't expect much from barista staff. If they don't manage to set themselves or the milk on fire while steaming my latte, I'll consider it good service. Sadly, the only thing steaming behind the counter today was this muppet and his attitude.

Without even a "howdy-do" we found ourselves in a sovietesque interrogation about what we could possibly want in his establishment. A question of "what tea would you recommend" was met with a sarcastic "it depends on your palette". We came here for some hot water, dried leaves and roasted beans... He could have suggested the worst item on the menu and we would gawked at his superior knowledge.

Now credit where credit is due, the drinks were prepared quickly. Which was perfect as we no longer felt welcome in this bourgeois palace of servitude. I dropped fifty cents in the ironically named "good karma" tip jar not because I thought this god among men was going to change the world with his unique take on customer service. No, it was because I felt sorry that he had to deal with common folk like us on a daily basis. The horror!

I'd like to think the other staff make up for his lack of service, but I certainly won't be back anytime soon to find out.

location.address: 1 Arashiyama Kamikawaracho, Nishikyo Ward, Kyoto, 616-0001, Japan

properties.review_text_published:
Hey westerners read this!

So this was my first onsen experience, and boy was it one to remember. First off, there is very little English in there so be prepared to speak a little to get info or do what I did and wait around watching people and then doing what they did.

Here's the process: put shoes in locker and take the key, use the machine to buy your day ticket and towels, take the tickets to the front desk and give them your shoe key. They'll give you the towels (if you bought them) and they'll hold on to your shoe key and give you a locker key.

From this point out its very simple, find your gender and strip down. I stood there awkwardly wondering where the showers were, but a nice guy directed me to them (they're inside the bathing area). And thats it... provided you know how to use an onsen (google it).

Overall it was a great experience and I'm glad I did it here as it was fairly low key and quiet. The staff was pretty nonchalant, but the baths were well kept and clean. People inside were quiet, I didn't talk to anyone... not that I could have anyways, either way I preferred the silence. The outdoor area was really nice, and the salt water bath was where I spend most of my time. Again, I had a great time and it was well worth the price. Highly recommend.

If you want to experience a capsule hotel or need a place to stay in-between THIS IS YOUR PLACE.

Seriously, very modern, friendly, and super clean. Walking around inside feels like your on the set for a sci-fi movie. The view from the 8th floor lobby is amazing too (see the image, seriously).

You also get two towels and some very comfortable lounge wear you sadly can't keep, but still very nice addition. The sleeping pods are comfortable, and they fit me (I'm 6 foot 5!), so no complaints there.

To be honest if we didn't have other places booked we would have stayed longer!

Not cool, which brings me to my next point, it gets hot in there... Literally.

Overall if you're going for the shows its a mixed bag, but otherwise seems like a pretty cool place... Which is something I thought I'd never say about a pole dancing place...

To be honest this was the best spot for pool and beer in Amsterdam that I could find. It's spacious, good quality tables and beer, plus the crowd is pretty friendly or failing that they're at least look friendly.

Let me tell you a story of our time at The Minds...

We're simple Canadian folk, looking for a bar one night. We like the off beat and we were told this was the place... And off beat it was.

The patrons looked like they were either just out of prison or on thier way to prison. Music was that of Metallica and ACDC or some other band, and the beer was cheap. It was pretty dam (heh) good!

If I ever come back to this city, you can find me at the pool table in The Minds.

properties.review_text_published:
They share much of the same beer/drink menu as Village Idiot next door, and I believe the kitchen as well.

Price wise, its pretty decent. You do pay a bit extra for the beer here as they serve half pints not full pints. Food is usually pretty good too.

It can be quiet here, but with OCAD just down the street be prepared to hear some freshman talk about how he just realized he can't get a job with a pottery and basket weaving diploma.

location.address: 126 McCaul St, Toronto, ON M5T 1W2, Canada
location.name: Village Idiot Pub

properties.review_text_published:
Great service, great beer selection, and cozy atmosphere.

This place has been a go-to on my list for a number of years. A fair bit of warning though, the glasses they use are half-pints and they charge close to double the base cost of the drink.

So if you like Beer X and it usually costs $4.00 for a full pint, you'll be paying close to $6 for a half pint here.

HOWEVER this is the kind of place you go to for beers that aren't usually aren't easy find. So choose one that you want to try and see how it goes... Experiment, just like my ex-girlfriend!

properties.review_text_published:
Ever gone to Hooters? Its like Hooters, but Scottish.

Service is good, even better if you like your waitress to be literally pouring out of her 2 sizes too small shirt. The beer selection is pretty average, and that's to be expected.

The atmosphere is pretty decent, again this is a chain. Expect a "traditional" feel and some booths. The best place to sit is actually outside on the patio in the summer. However this is a double edged sword as it's not inside, but you'll be in full view of the general public.

Overall if you're going to look up reviews on this place you're likely not the kind of person who this place is made for.
